metaData.originalTitle: 平平无奇的源码，竟藏着 Agent 的核心秘密？
metaData.title: Unremarkable Source Code Hides the Core Secret of Agents?
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article deeply dissects the core design of the Agent system by analyzing the OpenClaw source code: the layered assembly of System Prompts, the on-demand loading mechanism of Skills, and the Agent runtime loop, revealing key engineering practices of Agent architecture.
metaData.summary: In the form of a Tencent Cloud Developer official account article, this piece provides an in-depth interpretation of the source code for the OpenClaw Agent system. The author summarizes the Agent architecture as a "three-piece set": System Prompt, Agent runtime loop, and Skill mechanism. The article analyzes the layered structure of the System Prompt in detail, showing how it is assembled on demand from multiple independent modules (tools, security, skills, memory, etc.) like "Lego bricks." The core highlight is the Skill mechanism, which uses an "on-demand loading" strategy. Only the skill's name and description (approximately 100 tokens each) are injected into the System Prompt. When the LLM determines a skill is needed, it reads the complete SKILL.md file via a read tool, thus avoiding token waste from injecting all skill content at once. Additionally, the article introduces the SkillSnapshot mechanism, which prevents the loss of the skill directory due to context compression. The article also covers key designs such as the Agent runtime loop, heartbeat mechanism, sub-agent mechanism, Silent Reply, and context engine. Overall, this is a high-quality source code analysis article that provides valuable references for developers to understand the engineering implementation of Agent systems.

mainPoints.point: The Agent's System Prompt uses a layered, Lego-like assembly rather than a single hardcoded string.
mainPoints.explanation: Through the buildAgentSystemPrompt() function, modules like tools, security, skills, and memory are independently constructed and concatenated. It supports three modes: full, minimal, and none, enabling on-demand activation, which improves flexibility and token efficiency.

mainPoints.point: The core of the Skill mechanism is on-demand loading, which significantly saves initial token consumption.
mainPoints.explanation: The traditional approach injects all skill content into the prompt. In contrast, OpenClaw only injects the skill's name and description (approximately 100 tokens each) into the prompt. When the LLM determines a need, it reads the complete SKILL.md via a read tool. This saves approximately 98% of initial tokens compared to the traditional method.

mainPoints.point: The SkillSnapshot mechanism solves the problem of losing the skill directory due to context compression.
mainPoints.explanation: Each time the Agent runs, it rebuilds or uses an existing SkillSnapshot to inject into the prompt. This ensures that even after multiple rounds of conversation and context compression, the Agent always knows which skills are available.

keyQuotes: The large model has just one input variable. No matter how you encapsulate it, you're just concatenating strings.
The System Prompt is the script, Skills are expansion packs for the script, and the Agent Loop is the actor acting according to the script.

Traditional approach: Put all Skill content into the System Prompt → 20 Skills × 5000 tokens = 100,000 tokens (spent every time). OpenClaw approach: Phase 1 (every time): Only put name + description ≈ 100 tokens each.

relatedArticles.title: RAG is Dead? No, Grep is Back!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the leaked source code of Claude Code, this article deeply deconstructs its abandonment of RAG and vector retrieval in favor of an LLM-driven multi-round iterative Grep search mechanism. It compares this approach with Cursor and Codex, demonstrating the feasibility and design philosophy of a zero-index solution in code search scenarios.
